"""Closest pairs on closed simplices, evaluated by finite feature tests."""

from typing import Any

import warp as wp
from warp._src.context import register_api_function


@wp.func(inline=True)
def _segment_pair(p0: Any, p1: Any, q0: Any, q1: Any, scale_free: bool):
    zero = type(p0[0])(0.0)
    one = type(p0[0])(1.0)
    u = p1 - p0
    v = q1 - q0
    r = p0 - q0
    a = wp.dot(u, u)
    e = wp.dot(v, v)
    f = wp.dot(v, r)
    s = zero
    t = zero
    if a == zero:
        if e > zero:
            t = wp.clamp(f / e, zero, one)
    elif e == zero:
        s = wp.clamp(-wp.dot(u, r) / a, zero, one)
    else:
        b = wp.dot(u, v)
        c = wp.dot(u, r)
        # A cross product avoids subtracting nearly equal squared dot products
        # for near-parallel segments. In particular, do not collapse short or
        # nearly parallel but nondegenerate inputs with an absolute epsilon.
        # s is invariant to scaling v. In float32, using v / e keeps the
        # otherwise fourth-order products scale-free so they cannot under- or
        # overflow; float64 has the range and skips the extra work.
        w = v
        if scale_free:
            w = v * (one / e)
        n = wp.cross(u, w)
        denom = wp.dot(n, n)
        if denom > zero:
            s = wp.clamp(wp.dot(wp.cross(w, r), n) / denom, zero, one)
        t = (b * s + f) / e
        if t < zero:
            t = zero
            s = wp.clamp(-c / a, zero, one)
        elif t > one:
            t = one
            s = wp.clamp((b - c) / a, zero, one)
    delta = r + s * u - t * v
    return s, t, wp.dot(delta, delta)


@wp.func(inline=True)
def closest_points_seg_seg(p0: wp.vec3, p1: wp.vec3, q0: wp.vec3, q1: wp.vec3):
    """Return closest-point parameters and squared distance between two closed segments.

    Args:
        p0: First segment start.
        p1: First segment end.
        q0: Second segment start.
        q1: Second segment end.

    Returns:
        Tuple ``(s, t, distance_squared)``. The witnesses are
        ``p0 + s * (p1 - p0)`` and ``q0 + t * (q1 - q0)``, with both
        parameters in [0, 1]. A zero-length segment has parameter zero.
        Nonunique solutions select a deterministic pair for fixed input order.

    The selected branch is differentiable away from feature changes and ties.
    Derivatives at nonunique minima are branch derivatives, not unique geometric
    derivatives. No positive distance or length cutoff is applied. Inputs and
    squared lengths must be representable in the chosen precision; the
    float32 overload avoids higher-order products, so its accuracy does not
    depend on the overall scale of the inputs.
    """
    return _segment_pair(p0, p1, q0, q1, True)


@wp.func(inline=True)
def closest_points_seg_seg(p0: wp.vec3d, p1: wp.vec3d, q0: wp.vec3d, q1: wp.vec3d):
    return _segment_pair(p0, p1, q0, q1, False)


@wp.func(inline=True)
def _triangle_segment(a: Any, b: Any, c: Any, p: Any, q: Any):
    zero = type(a[0])(0.0)
    one = type(a[0])(1.0)
    ab = b - a
    ac = c - a
    direction = q - p
    n = wp.cross(ab, ac)
    nn = wp.dot(n, n)
    if nn > zero:
        # The closest point on the segment to the supporting plane is globally
        # optimal if its projection lies in the triangle. Otherwise a closest
        # pair exists on a triangle edge (also when parallel to the plane).
        height = wp.dot(n, p - a)
        slope = wp.dot(n, direction)
        t = zero
        if slope != zero:
            t = wp.clamp(-height / slope, zero, one)
        offset = (p - a) + t * direction
        v = wp.dot(wp.cross(offset, ac), n) / nn
        w = wp.dot(wp.cross(ab, offset), n) / nn
        # Test the returned weight itself: v + w <= 1 can hold after rounding
        # while one - v - w is still slightly negative.
        u = one - v - w
        if u >= zero and v >= zero and w >= zero:
            bary = type(a)(u, v, w)
            delta = v * ab + w * ac - offset
            return bary, t, wp.dot(delta, delta)

    s, t, best = closest_points_seg_seg(a, b, p, q)
    bary = type(a)(one - s, s, zero)
    edge_s, edge_t, d2 = closest_points_seg_seg(b, c, p, q)
    if d2 < best:
        bary = type(a)(zero, one - edge_s, edge_s)
        t = edge_t
        best = d2
    edge_s, edge_t, d2 = closest_points_seg_seg(c, a, p, q)
    if d2 < best:
        bary = type(a)(edge_s, zero, one - edge_s)
        t = edge_t
        best = d2
    return bary, t, best


@wp.func(inline=True)
def closest_points_tri_seg(a: wp.vec3, b: wp.vec3, c: wp.vec3, p: wp.vec3, q: wp.vec3):
    """Return closest-point coordinates and squared distance for a triangle and segment.

    Args:
        a: First triangle vertex.
        b: Second triangle vertex.
        c: Third triangle vertex.
        p: Segment start.
        q: Segment end.

    Returns:
        Tuple ``(bary, t, distance_squared)``. The witnesses are
        ``bary[0]*a + bary[1]*b + bary[2]*c`` and ``p + t*(q-p)``.
        Barycentric coordinates are nonnegative and sum to one; ``t`` lies in
        [0, 1]. Degenerate triangles are treated as the union of their edges.

    This finite feature query includes piercing, coplanar, and boundary cases.
    Nonunique minima use deterministic input-order tie breaking. Derivatives
    follow the selected branch away from feature changes; they are not unique
    at ties. No geometric tolerance is applied. Inputs and intermediate products
    must be representable in the chosen precision, including the squared
    triangle normal, which grows with the fourth power of the edge lengths: in
    float32, edge lengths outside roughly [1e-9, 1e9] can make a nondegenerate
    triangle be treated as degenerate.
    """
    return _triangle_segment(a, b, c, p, q)


@wp.func(inline=True)
def closest_points_tri_seg(a: wp.vec3d, b: wp.vec3d, c: wp.vec3d, p: wp.vec3d, q: wp.vec3d):
    return _triangle_segment(a, b, c, p, q)


register_api_function(closest_points_seg_seg, module="warp.geometry", python_callable=True, differentiable=True)
register_api_function(closest_points_tri_seg, module="warp.geometry", python_callable=True, differentiable=True)

import importlib.util
from pathlib import Path
import sys
import json
import hashlib
import numpy as np
import warp as wp
import warp.geometry

root=Path('/home/horde/Repos/warp.intersection')
def load(name,path):
    spec=importlib.util.spec_from_file_location(name,path)
    mod=importlib.util.module_from_spec(spec);sys.modules[name]=mod;spec.loader.exec_module(mod);return mod
base=load('closest_review_baseline','/tmp/closest_review_baseline.py')
src=(root/'asv/benchmarks/closest_points.py').read_text()
src=src.replace('def make_kernel(method, triangle, contact=False, precision="float32", capsule=True):', '''def make_kernel(method, triangle, contact=False, precision="float32", capsule=True, impl=wp.geometry):
    tri_func = impl.closest_points_tri_seg
    seg_func = impl.closest_points_seg_seg''')
src=src.replace('wp.geometry.closest_points_tri_seg(a, b, c, p, q)', 'tri_func(a, b, c, p, q)').replace('wp.geometry.closest_points_seg_seg(a, b, p, q)', 'seg_func(a, b, p, q)')
Path('/tmp/closest_review_benchmark_module.py').write_text(src)
bench=load('closest_review_benchmark_module','/tmp/closest_review_benchmark_module.py')
wp.init();count=262144;rows=[]
for triangle in [False,True]:
    for name in ['random','near','parallel','separated','degenerate']:
        raw=bench.workload(count,name)
        data=wp.array(raw,dtype=wp.vec3,device='cuda:0');graphs={};outputs={}
        for label,mod in [('reviewed',base),('rescaled',wp.geometry)]:
            out=wp.empty(count,dtype=wp.types.vector(8,wp.float32),device='cuda:0');outputs[label]=out
            graphs[label]=bench.capture(bench.make_kernel('warp',triangle,impl=mod),[data,out],count)
        rounds=[bench.graph_times(graphs) for _ in range(3)]
        row=dict(primitive='tri' if triangle else 'seg', workload=name, rounds_us=rounds, median_us={k:float(np.median([r[k] for r in rounds])) for k in graphs}, max_sdf_delta=float(np.max(np.abs(outputs['reviewed'].numpy()[:,3]-outputs['rescaled'].numpy()[:,3]))))
        print(json.dumps(row),flush=True);rows.append(row)
Path('/tmp/closest-review-timings.json').write_text(json.dumps(dict(device=wp.get_device('cuda:0').name,count=count,samples=21,launches=30,rounds=3,baseline_sha256=hashlib.sha256(Path('/tmp/closest-review-baseline.py').read_bytes()).hexdigest(),implementation_sha256=hashlib.sha256((root/'warp/_src/geometry/closest.py').read_bytes()).hexdigest(),results=rows),indent=2)+'\n')
